transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, what made me make the appointment is... I just feel like the warm part of me has completely shut off. I'll get home from work and sit with my husband, or try to watch my shows, and I know I should feel some comfort or at least a little happy to be relaxing. But there’s just nothing there. I just don't feel any of those good things right now.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been about three weeks now. It started right after... well, there was an accident at work. A pallet collapsed and injured my coworker. I've just been feeling this way ever since that happened.
Since the accident, have you been experiencing unwanted memories or images of what happened popping into your mind?

Yeah, I do. It happens out of nowhere, really. I'll just... I'll see that pallet coming down again, or I'll hear that loud crash in my head. It's especially bad at work if a forklift beeps or somebody drops something heavy in the warehouse. Whenever that happens, my stomach just completely turns.
Have you found yourself going out of your way to avoid places, people, or thoughts that remind you of the accident?

No, not really. I mean, I still have to go to work and be in the warehouse every day, so I'm right in the same area where it happened. I haven't been staying away from any specific places or the people I work with. I don't think I'm going out of my way to avoid anything... I just try to get through my shifts.
Have you noticed feeling constantly on edge, jumpy, or unusually startled by everyday sounds or surprises?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, especially when I’m anywhere near the receiving area now, I'm just constantly on edge. I find myself always checking the racks, looking at the pallet heights, figuring out exactly where the exits are... and I'm always checking to see who’s moving behind me. It's just like I can’t trust the floor to be safe for even a minute anymore.
Have you felt a sense of unreality, like you are in a dream or disconnected from your surroundings?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. Everything feels pretty real to me... maybe a little too real sometimes, with how much I'm paying attention to everything now. But no, I don't feel like I'm in a dream or disconnected from what's going on around me.
Do you find yourself trying to push away or avoid thoughts, feelings, or memories about the accident?

Not really, no. I actually think about it pretty often. Since I'm right back in the warehouse every day, it's... it's kind of hard not to think about it, honestly. I don't really try to block it out or push the memories away. They just sort of pop up on their own while I'm working.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed emotional blunting, hypervigilance, and intrusive memories following an occupational accident three weeks ago. However, the patient explicitly denies behavioral or cognitive avoidance, and symptom duration is under one month, falling short of the full criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder (F43.1) and exceeding the brief time frame typical of acute stress reaction (F43.0). Consequently, an adjustment disorder (F43.2) is the most accurate ICD-10 diagnosis.
